plain_english_policy: HB197 (2011) shifts Alabama’s pesticide regulation system toward a **two-year biennial registration cycle** and establishes a tiered fee structure to fund state oversight. The bill does not alter core safety or environmental restrictions but **increases administrative burden on registrants** while generating more revenue for the Agricultural Fund.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The bill reflects a **pro-regulatory, cost-recovery approach** with these key effects if enacted:
evidence_quotes: registration shall be renewed annually... **The fee shall be paid according to the schedule in subsection (i).** The fee structure shall remain in effect until October 1, 2011, and thereafter in no event shall the product registration fee exceed the national average...
**All registrations issued by the department pursuant to subsection (a) shall be biennial** upon payment of a fee of four hundred dollars ($400) per product.
The fee shall accompany the application for registration and be deposited to the credit of the Agricultural Fund of the State Treasury.
review_reason: No ambiguity in text; no ceremonial/appropriations-only language. Directly alters administrative process and fee structure.
